scenario: Attacker escalates to domain admin and deploys ransomware domain-wide
treatment: Privileged Access Management; tiered admin model; LAPS; remove standing admin rights

scenario: Attacker deletes or encrypts backups before detonation
treatment: 3-2-1-1-0 strategy; immutable/air-gapped copy; separate backup credentials with MFA

scenario: Exploitation of known CVEs on edge devices and web servers
treatment: 72-hour SLA for actively exploited CVEs (CISA KEV); attack-surface scanning

scenario: Attacker uses stolen credentials on VPN/RDP exposed to the internet
treatment: Phishing-resistant MFA; close public RDP; geo/IP restrictions

scenario: Data stolen before encryption and leaked to force payment
treatment: Data classification; DLP; egress filtering; encryption at rest

scenario: Intrusion goes unnoticed for days before encryption
treatment: Central SIEM; MDR/SOC 24/7; alerts for mass file changes and backup tampering

scenario: Recovery not prioritised by business criticality
treatment: Complete BIA; define RTO/RPO; rank systems for restoration

scenario: Backups fail or are slow to restore when needed
treatment: Quarterly restore tests; verify integrity and malware-free before restore

scenario: Stolen browser-saved credentials sold and used for access
treatment: Password manager; MFA everywhere; dark-web credential monitoring

scenario: Vendor or MSP compromised and used to push ransomware
treatment: Vendor risk assessments; security clauses; least-privilege vendor access

scenario: Unpatchable systems are easy targets and halt operations when encrypted
treatment: Isolate legacy systems; virtual patching; compensating controls

scenario: Scans run irregularly; findings not prioritised by exploitability
treatment: Continuous scanning; risk-based prioritisation; remediation tracking KPIs

risk: Poor crisis communication and legal notification
scenario: Delayed regulator/customer/staff notification causes fines and reputational loss
treatment: Comms plan; legal counsel on call; regulatory notification matrix

scenario: Employee opens malicious attachment/link that drops a loader and ransomware
treatment: Monthly phishing simulations; email sandboxing; report-phish button

scenario: Ransomware spreads rapidly across servers and workstations
treatment: Segment crown jewels; restrict SMB/RDP east-west; micro-segmentation

risk: No EDR on endpoints and servers
scenario: Ransomware executes undetected on unmanaged or legacy-AV hosts
treatment: Deploy EDR with ransomware behaviour rules and auto-isolation

scenario: Slow, uncoordinated response increases dwell time and damage
treatment: Ransomware playbook; biannual tabletop exercises; IR retainer

scenario: Recovery of critical systems takes weeks
treatment: Update DR plan; restoration runbooks; clean-room recovery environment

scenario: Unknown systems stay unpatched and unmonitored, becoming entry points
treatment: Automated discovery; CMDB; owner assigned to each asset

scenario: Same weaknesses repeat across incidents
treatment: Mandatory lessons-learned reviews; track corrective actions

scenario: Weak oversight leads to underfunded controls and unclear risk appetite
treatment: Quarterly board reporting; documented cyber risk appetite; KPIs/KRIs

scenario: Ad hoc payment decision without legal, sanctions or insurance review
treatment: Documented decision framework; sanctions screening; cyber insurance review
